From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: 95p latency spike & 5xx errors on reserved capacity — FastPay (urgent)

On it — quick notes from initial triage: 
- Pool metrics (us-west-2, pool FP-reserved-3) show steady GPU utilization at ~94% with input queue depth climbing at the 08:50–09:10 window. Kernel queue latency and KV cache misses increased concurrently. No recent model binary deploys in the pool during that window.
- We see a surge in very long sequences from the customer's traffic pattern (checkout risk-scorer batching), causing longer per-request processing. Batching thresholds currently tuned for lower seq lengths; larger seqs increase per-token cost and slow batching throughput.
- No obvious infra fault (disk/GPU mem fine). Autoscaler did not trigger extra nodes because the policy is conservative for reserved pools.

Immediate mitigation options I can enact in the next 15–30m:
1) Temporarily widen batching timeout to reduce queueing at cost of a small increase in median latency — will lower per-token throughput pressure.
2) Route a percentage (20–40%) of FastPay traffic to a compatible hosted variant with looser capacity limits for short window (requires consent + change to routing policy).
3) Emergency increase: spin an extra reserved instance from burst quota if available (needs ops approval; may take ~8–12m to attach).

I'll implement option 1 right away and run a 20m stabilization test. If we still see >1s 95p after that, request option 2 or 3. Uploading a microtrace and pool dashboard links to Jira.

—Dylan
SRE (Serving) — Redwood Inference
Attachment: pool_microtrace_08-55-09-10.txt

Thanks for the rapid triage. A few thoughts and asks from exec/ops side:

- Approve up to one hour of free burst capacity (ops-approved) to stabilize; finance will reconcile credits against the contract if SLA breach confirmed. Marissa — please estimate credit exposure if we fall into SLA credit territory.
- Post-incident: we need a small cross-functional RCA focusing on reserved-pool autoscale policy and batching defaults for customers with variable sequence distributions. Schedule a 60m sync tomorrow with SRE, Product, and Sales.

Dylan — proceed with the changes you recommended and update this thread with stabilization metrics. If transient fixes fail, escalate to spin an extra reserved instance immediately.
